notes: Decided privacy-enforcement outcomes. Each record is a real matter with a source URL. 'statutory_cap_at_decision' is the ceiling that applied when the decision was taken, given only where it can be computed from public financials, and always labelled as an estimate in cap_basis - it is what turns raw amounts into comparable ratios. 'verification' records how the figure was checked: primary-verified (read at the enforcer's own site or in legislation), secondary-reported (multiple independent reports, enforcer page not individually linked), unverified-in-prototype.

precedents.instrument: GDPR Art. 46(1) (transfers to the US without appropriate safeguards)
precedents.violation_summary: Continued transfers of EU/EEA personal data to the US on the basis of the invalidated Privacy Shield / SCCs without supplementary measures, following the Schrems II judgment.
precedents.cap_basis: 4% of Meta FY2022 total revenue (US$116.6bn, from the company's annual report) converted at the 2022 average rate gives roughly EUR 109.6bn of turnover and a ceiling near EUR 4.4bn - an estimate, not a figure published by the DPC

source.quality: regulator decisions register

precedents.notes: Largest GDPR fine on record. Amount/ceiling ratio is about 0.27 - the highest observed in this dataset.

precedents.cap_basis: ByteDance's worldwide turnover is not published, so no turnover-linked ceiling can be computed

precedents.notes: Contributes to the absolute award band for transfers cases but not to ratio calibration (no computable ceiling).

precedents.instrument: CCPA - failure to disclose sale and to honour opt-out via global privacy controls
precedents.violation_summary: Sold personal information without disclosure, failed to process opt-out requests made through user-enabled global privacy controls, and failed to cure within 30 days.

source.quality: enforcer press release

precedents.notes: First CCPA enforcement settlement. $1.2m is equivalent to 480 violations at $2,500 - the pleaded class was far larger, which is why the settlement-to-ceiling calibration in this model exists.

precedents.instrument: CCPA - sharing health-related data through tracking technology without opt-out
precedents.violation_summary: Use of online tracking technology on a health information site shared data suggesting a consumer may have a serious health condition, without allowing opt-out; novel term bans sharing article titles that reveal a diagnosis.

source.quality: enforcer enforcement-actions register (with the accompanying stipulated judgment PDF at oag.ca.gov)

precedents.notes: The closest US analogue to a consumer-health-app pixel case, and therefore a strong comparator for health-sector cases.

precedents.violation_summary: Participation in marketing co-operatives treated as a sale of personal information without notice or opt-out; data later reached a data broker.

precedents.violation_summary: Twenty-one mobile games offered no CCPA-compliant opt-out, and data of consumers aged 13-16 was sold or shared without the required affirmative consent.

precedents.instrument: Texas CUBI (and the state's biometric privacy framework)
precedents.violation_summary: Capture and use of millions of Texans' biometric identifiers without the notice and consent required by CUBI.
